previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mrs. ___ was admitted for intractable nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, dysphagia, and odynophagia, all stemming from severe radiation esophagitis related to prior treatment for tracheal cancer. Despite a recent hospitalization and treatment with high-dose pantoprazole and fluconazole, her symptoms progressed, leading to poor oral intake and dehydration. A CT scan showed worsening esophageal wall thickening, and GI consultation confirmed she was not a candidate for dilation due to severe ulceration. A percutaneous endoscopic jejunostomy (PEJ) tube was placed to enable enteral feeding and allow the esophagus to heal. Her nausea and vomiting resolved post-procedure, and pain was managed with adjusted opioid dosing. A prednisone taper was initiated for rheumatoid arthritis, and nortriptyline was started for neuropathic pain. She was discharged home with nursing services, a detailed medication regimen, and plans for outpatient GI follow-up to reassess for dilation in several weeks.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ female with history of multiple cancers (breast,
lung, tracheal), now presenting with chest pain and shortness of breath as
well as abdominal pain and tenderness.  Abdominal tenderness is diffuse, most
prominent in the left lower quadrant.  Assess for evidence of pulmonary
embolism or diverticulitis.

COMPARISON:  Multiple chest CTs with the latest one being CT chest with
contrast on ___.  CTA of the chest and CT of the abdomen and
pelvis were performed on ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Helical MDCT images were acquired through the chest before and
after the uneventful administration of IV contrast.  Imaging through the chest
was performed per chest pain protocol with optimized opacification of the
aorta and pulmonary arteries.  Initial portal venous phase delay was performed
through the abdomen.  Scanning was performed through the abdomen and pelvis
per clinical concern.  Multiplanar reformatted images were generated of both
the chest and abdominal pelvic datasets.

FINDINGS:

CHEST:  Again noted are post-surgical changes of prior right upper lobectomy. 
Post-radiation changes in the in the anterior right hemithorax and the
paramediastinal left upper lobe are stable.  There is a new area of
consolidation in the right lower lobe (3A:33) as well as other scattered
nodluar opacities, ___ in the superior segment of th right lower lobe.  The
previously noted opacification in the superior segment of the left lower lobe
is more conspicuous in this exam (3a:41). Multiple ground-glass opacities are
noted in the right lung (3A:35), which are essentially unchanged compared with
___. A small right sided pleural effusion is stable or minimally
increased from prior exam.

A subcarinal soft tissue mass measuring 1.8 x 1.6 cm (3A:37) appears unchanged
compared with previous study.  The tracheal lumen shows a lateral projection
(3A:17) that might represent a large ulcer or pseudo-diverticulum due to
scarring, as previously described.  The esophageal wall is thickened
throughout consistent with history of radiation esophagitis, tumor
infiltration not excluded. The heart is mildly enlarged and there is no
pericardial effusion.

Dystrophic calcification and ill-defined scarring seen within the right
breast.

CTA THORAX: There is no main, right, left, or lobar pulmonary artery filling
defect concerning for pulmonary embolism.  Segmental and subsegmental vessels
are not well seen secondary to phase of contrast and patient respiratory
motion.  The main pulmonary artery is normal in size and the thoracic aorta is
normal in caliber without aneurysm or dissection.

ABDOMEN AND PELVIS:  A Gastrojejunostomy tube again seen. The liver, pancreas
and spleen are unremarkable noting some limitation from respiratory motion. 
There is no intrahepatic biliary dilatation.  Both kidneys enhance
symmetrically with no hydronephrosis.  The gallbladder is present, but
incompletely distended with no wall thickening or pericholecystic inflammation
is noted.  

The intra-abdominal vasculature is unremarkable.  There are no retroperitoneal
or mesenteric lymph node enlargement.  Areas of the rectosigmoid are collapsed
and not well evaluated.  No free air or abdominal wall hernias are noted.
There is no bowel obstruction. A normal appendix is identified.  There is
possible wall thickening in an area of the sigmoid that is not well distended,
but there is no evidence of diverticulitis.  Trace of fluid is noted in the
pelvis.  

PELVIC CT: The urinary bladder is unremarkable. No pelvic wall or inguinal
lymph node enlargement is seen. The uterus and ovaries are age appropriate and
unremarkable. There are ovoid fluid attenuation foci surrounding the urethra
at the base of the bladder, which were present in prior exam and represent
urethral diverticula.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  An old fracture of the right 7th rib is again seen, as
well as a grade 2 anterolisthesis of L4 on L5 with extensive L4-L5 disk
degeneration and vacuum phenomenon.  No suspicious osseous lesions seen.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No central pulmonary embolism.  Segmental and subsegmental vessels were
not seen due to phase of contrast and respiratory motion..
2.  Interval development of new right lower lobe nodular consolidation
concerning for infection/inflammation given rapid interval development.
3.  No interval change in appearance of tracheal wall thickening and
irregulatry, esophageal wall thickening, and mediastinal nodes.
4.  Diverticulosis without clear diverticulitis.  Area of possible apparent
focal wall thickening in a nondistended portion of the sigmoid, which may
relate to underdistention, however further evaluation with sigmoidoscopy could
further delineate.
